linked_issues.body: ## Summary A connection drop during an outgoing Arkade Lightning send can strand funds: the input VTXO is marked spent (pending) but the send never finalizes, so the output never becomes a spendable VTXO. Balance drops to 0, nothing shows in pending, and recovery needs the operator to re-serve the pending tx. Root cause: our `ArkadeRemoteIdentity` signs checkpoints one-at-a-time (serialized MuSig2 round-trips) *between* `submitTx` and `finalizeTx`, creating a long window where a dropped connection leaves the tx half-finalized. ## Why / Reasoning **Incident (mainnet, release/v0.87.0):** bought BTC → arrived on Arkade boarding → paid a ~28.6k-sat Lightning invoice → confirmed with passkey → balance dropped to 0, money didn't arrive, no pending tx shown. ~72.5k sats stranded. **Trace (verified against `arkade.computer` indexer + Boltz):** - Input VTXO `0bf0f1d7…:0` (72,501): `isSpent=true`, `spentBy=fe6793a3…`, still returned under `pendingOnly=true`. - Spending ark tx `e0726e…` was **submitted but never finalized**. Its output checkpoint `46c2ea…` was never indexed as a spendable VTXO (`/vtxos?outpoints=fe6793a3…:0` → `[]`). - The tx had **16 inputs → 16 checkpoints**. **Root cause — signing architecture:** - `ArkadeRemoteIdentity` is a MuSig2 2-of-2 (client + `arkade.nuri.com` server), client key unlocked via WebAuthn passkey PRF. Every signature is an interactive MuSig2 nonce round-trip. - It does **not** implement `signMultiple`, so the SDK's `isBatchSignable()` is false and the batch fast-path is skipped. - On the non-batch path the SDK signs the arkTx before `submitTx`, then signs each checkpoint **after** `submitTx` via `Promise.all(checkpoints.map(sign))`. Our `signingKeyVault.runSignExclusive` (single-flight `signOpTail` queue) then **serializes** those. So 16 checkpoints = 16 sequential MuSig2 round-trips sitting between `submitTx` and `finalizeTx`. - The connection dropped in that window → `finalizeTx` never ran → half-finalized checkpoint. **Secondary finding — no client self-recovery:** - The app never auto-runs `finalizePendingTxs` (only our new debug button does). - `finalizePendingTxs` short-circuits on a single **global** `hasPendingTx` boolean; a later successful send clears it, erasing the "interrupted send" marker. So even the SDK's designed recovery never fires. **Recovery performed (proves the diagnosis):** Arkade re-served the pending tx on `/v1/tx/pending`; we finalized client-side (intent built over the spent input + force-set the pending flag — debug tooling). 50,493 change returned immediately; 28,609 landed in the Boltz VHTLC (swap `FktQNozCtAY6`, invoice expired) → recoverable via the `refundWithoutReceiver` CLTV on 2026-07-13. ## Decisions - **Primary fix:** implement `signMultiple` on `ArkadeRemoteIdentity` (+ batched MuSig2 nonce exchange with the cosigner server). In the SDK batch path *all* signing (arkTx + every checkpoint) happens up front before `submitTx`; finalize only `combineTapscriptSigs`. Result: **zero client round-trips between `submitTx` and `finalizeTx`** → the interruption window is removed. - **Secondary:** auto-run `finalizePendingTxs` on launch/foreground, and replace the global `hasPendingTx` boolean with a per-tx pending record so a later send can't erase an unfinalized one. ## Trade-offs / Risks - MuSig2 batched nonce handling must be correct — no secret-nonce reuse across the batch. The current serialization exists partly for nonce safety + single-flight passkey; batching must preserve those invariants. - `_signerRouter.canBatch(...)` must also return true for the batch path to engage — verify our router reports batch capability. - Auto-running `finalizePendingTxs` at launch adds a signed `/v1/tx/pending` call (passkey scope) on startup when a pending marker exists — gate it so it only runs when needed. ## Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph now[Current — non-batch] A1[sign arkTx] --> A2[submitTx] --> A3[sign 16 checkpoints\nserialized MuSig2 round-trips] --> A4[finalizeTx]

prompt_context.issue_body: ## Problem (measured post-#28) Single-flight (#28) killed the concurrent pile-up, but `/receive/sync` still sat at ~6s per pass. Traced to the prod DB: every **`invoice.settled`** row is force-live-refreshed on every sync — one owner has **55** settled rows. The host confirmed Boltz status calls run ~serially, so N settled rows ≈ N×~550ms ≈ ~6s. `#27` only skipped **dead** rows (expired/failed/refunded). `invoice.settled` is not dead, so settled receives are re-fetched forever. ## Change (`src/ArkadeReceive.js`) Settled is terminal Boltz-side (`invoice.settled` never reverts), and a settled swap's claimable-vs-claimed state comes from the **Arkade indexer** (one batched call), not Boltz. So: - Exclude settled rows from the Boltz `fetchStatuses` call (and `forceLive`). - In the prepared loop, settled rows trust their **stored** status (`fromCache=true`, no writeback) → still resolve to `"settled"` → still get the **same indexer claim check**. Live-fetched set shrinks to genuinely-active swaps (`swap.created`/`mempool`/`confirmed`), usually 1–2 → pass drops from ~6s toward ~1s. ## Safety (money-adjacent) - **No funds-visibility change.** Claimable-vs-claimed is still decided by the live indexer call **every** sync: settled+unspent → `claimable` (shown), settled+spent → hidden. Only the redundant Boltz *status* re-fetch is skipped. - First settlement is still discovered live (a row only enters the skip path once its stored status is already `invoice.settled`). - Indexer unavailable → settled rows still surface as claimable (fail-safe, unchanged). - Claim approval unchanged (still gated by `verifyArkadePsbtSignRequests`; lockup txids still collected from `stored.response` + live reverse-tx probe). ## Tests `proof:receive`: `settledUnspentStatus: claimable`, `settledSpentHidden: true`, claim `signStatus 200` / `deniedStatus 403`. `proof:pending-swaps` 18/18, `proof:local` green. ## Deploy / rollback `deployment_version` 6 → 7. linked_issues.body: ## Problem Two related enforcement gaps, verified in react-native-keychain 10.0.0 source: **1. Android silently stores wallet keys with no auth requirement when no strong biometrics exist.** `KeychainModule.kt` computes `useBiometry = getUseBiometry(accessControl) && (isFingerprintAuthAvailable || isFaceAuthAvailable || isIrisAuthAvailable)`. On devices without strong (Class 3) biometrics, auth-requiring cipher storages are skipped and the key is stored under a no-auth AES-GCM keystore key. The write succeeds, reads never prompt. `securityLevel: SECURE_HARDWARE` does not prevent this (it only validates TEE-backing). **2. The app lock has no authentication mechanism of its own.** `BiometricLockModal` "unlocks" by reading the stored private key via `getPrivateKey()`. Consequences: - Android (no biometrics): the auto-unlock keychain read succeeds instantly → lock dismisses itself, no gate at all. - Android (with biometrics): the keystore key accepts `AUTH_BIOMETRIC_STRONG or AUTH_DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` with a 5s validity window, and timeout-based keys are satisfied by the device unlock itself — reopening the app shortly after unlocking the phone typically passes with no prompt. - The lock is coupled to persisted keys, so it cannot survive the planned stateless-signing migration (see follow-up issue). ## Tasks ### Android storage fallback (lib/secureKeyStorage.ts) - [ ] In the biometric-protected writers (`storePrivateKey`, `storeNostrPrivateKey`, `storeAuthKey`): on Android, when `getSupportedBiometryType()` returns null, use `ACCESS_CONTROL.DEVICE_PASSCODE` instead of `BIOMETRY_CURRENT_SET` (maps to `usePasscode = true` → auth-requiring storage with device-credential prompt). - [ ] If the device has no lock screen at all (passcode storage also unavailable — library would silently fall through to no-auth again), throw instead of storing. ### Standalone app lock (components/BiometricLockModal.tsx) - [ ] Replace the `getPrivateKey()`-based unlock with `expo-local-authentication` `authenticateAsync({ disableDeviceFallback: true })` — biometric-only on both platforms (LAContext on iOS, BIOMETRIC_STRONG-only BiometricPrompt on Android), decoupled from key storage. - [ ] On devices without biometrics, fall back to a device-credential prompt (`disableDeviceFallback: false`), consistent with the storage fallback above. - [ ] New dependency: `expo-local-authentication`. ## Non-goals - No custom native module for true biometric-only keystore keys on Android (`setUserAuthenticationParameters(0, AUTH_BIOMETRIC_STRONG)` + enrollment invalidation) — not worth hardening a storage layer slated for removal by stateless signing. - iOS broken-biometrics lockout flow (30s auto-logout + wipe) stays as is.

prompt_context.issue_body: ## Summary Replaces native passkey ceremonies and React Native `<Modal>` overlays with the PWA's approach: WebView-based WebAuthn PRF and z-index layer overlays. Same direction as the PWA — one web context, one source of truth — shipped as an OTA-safe JS change (native PasskeyModule left dormant, runtimeVersion fingerprint unchanged). ## Passkey: WebView ceremonies - **`WebAuthnPrfService.ts`** (new) — Promise-bridge that lets non-UI code request a PRF/assertion the same way it used to call the native module. Public functions have byte-identical signatures/return shapes to the old native service, so call-sites swap imports 1:1. Each call registers a pending `{resolve, reject}` and emits `webauthn:prfRequest`; the always-mounted overlay runs the ceremony and resolves it. - **`WebAuthnPrfOverlay.tsx`** (new) — global overlay listening for `webauthn:prfRequest`, mounting `PasskeyWebAuthnPrfView`. - **`PasskeyNativeModuleService.ts`** — gutted to a thin re-export of the three bridge functions (`createWalletPasskey`, `useExistingWalletPasskey`, `getWalletPasskeyAssertion`). Native module no longer called at runtime. - **`PasskeyNativeModuleService.web.ts`** — web/PWA path calls `navigator.credentials` directly; same three functions. - Removed the now-callerless combined `useExistingWalletPasskeyWithAssertion` and its dead `prfAssertion` variant machinery. ## Signing: hold key in memory - **`signingKeyVault.ts`** / **`ArkadeRemoteIdentity.ts`** — derive the signing key via PRF once at bootstrap and hold it session-resident (`preObtained`), dropping per-operation PRF re-derivation. Adds arming for one-tap receive-claim and LNURL register where the challenge is pre-fetchable. ## Modals → layers - **`LayerHost.tsx`** (new) — portal that renders overlays as z-index `View` layers (zIndex 100000), so overlays compose like PWA DOM layers instead of native `<Modal>`. - Converted `ModalSheet`, `FullScreenModal`, `BiometricRetryModal`, `PleaseUpdateAppModal`, `SumsubWebModal`, `LegacySafeMigrationCard` from `<Modal>` to `<Layer>`. ## One-tap flows - **`PaymentReceivedModal.tsx`**, **`UsernameOnboardingScreen.tsx`** — prefetch the auth challenge and run the passkey ceremony via a transparent overlay WebView on the real button, collapsing the button→confirm double-tap into one tap. ## Other - **`PasskeyLoginScreen*`** — WebView login screen + i18n (`en.ts`/`de.ts`). - **`MoneriumService.ts`**, **`secureKeyStorage*`**, **`lib/web/*`** — web shim/keychain plumbing for the PWA build. - **`public/index.html`** / status bar — `black-translucent` for full-bleed layout. - **`stages.ts`**, **`DebugMigrationLabModal.tsx`** — migration + migration-lab use `getWalletPasskeyAssertion` directly. <!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai --> ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added a new passkey/WebAuthn flow with on-screen overlays for creating, using, and confirming passkeys. * Introduced a unified layering system for dialogs and full-screen sheets, improving how overlays appear above the app. * Updated the passkey login screen with clearer wording and refreshed button labels. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved passkey and biometric dialogs to behave more reliably across devices. * Adjusted full-screen and payment-related flows to better handle dismissals, focus, and status bar display. <!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

linked_issues.body: ## Summary Boarding sweep approve currently can reuse the same WebAuthn/PRF request-auth assertion to mint multiple exact `approval_token`s, as long as the request-auth token has not expired. That works today, but it is implicit replay. Add an explicit short-lived `boarding_sweep_session_token`, matching the LN claim pattern, so the wallet gets one OS/passkey prompt per boarding sweep and then mints later exact approval tokens without replaying WebAuthn fields. ## Current backend behavior Endpoint: ```http POST /api/arkade/receive/boarding/sweep/approve ``` Code path: - `src/ArkadeServer.js#handleReceiveBoardingSweepApprove` - always calls `verifyRequestAuth(body, cfg)` - then validates the sweep via `requireBoardingSweepApprovalContext` - then issues a `spend_approval` token with: - `state: boarding_sweep:${sweep.stateDigest}` - exact `requestKeys` - exact `treeTxids` - `approvalScope: "boarding_sweep"` Important: backend does **not** consume request-auth/WebAuthn assertions. So one `token + client_data_b64u + auth_data_b64u + sig_b64u` can currently be reused for multiple boarding sweep approve calls until `TOKEN_TTL` expires. That means the wallet can currently do: 1. get one WebAuthn assertion 2. call `/boarding/sweep/approve` for exact direct requests 3. reuse the same request-auth fields 4. call `/boarding/sweep/approve` again for exact tree requests Each response still returns a fresh exact `approval_token`. ## Problem Relying on reusable WebAuthn request-auth is not obvious and is different from LN claim UX. LN claim already has explicit session semantics: - first approve uses WebAuthn - response includes `claim_session_token` - later approve calls use the session token - every returned `approval_token` remains exact scoped Boarding sweep should be the same. ## Desired behavior Add explicit boarding sweep approval sessions: 1. First `/api/arkade/receive/boarding/sweep/approve` uses WebAuthn request auth. 2. Response includes: - exact `approval_token` for current request batch - `boarding_sweep_session_token` - `boarding_sweep_session_expires_at_ms` 3. Later approve calls for the same sweep send `boarding_sweep_session_token` instead of WebAuthn fields. 4. Server re-runs full boarding sweep validation every call. 5. Server returns a fresh exact `approval_token` for each batch. 6. `boarding_sweep_session_token` must not work as `/arkade/sign` approval. Keep approval tokens exact. Do **not** broaden `spend_approval`. ## Server implementation sketch Mirror `claim_session_token` with minimal changes. ### 1. prompt_context.issue_body: ## What `verifyToken` compared the base64url HMAC tag with string `!==`, which short-circuits at the first differing character. Over a low-jitter path (same host / colo / SSRF) this leaks how long a prefix an attacker-submitted tag shares with the real one — a timing oracle on token forgery. `verifyToken` is the single primitive behind **every** auth path: - `spend_approval` (direct signing — `/arkade/sign`, tree, v5 send) - `boarding_sweep_session` / `receive_claim_session` / `recoverable_session` session tokens - `confirm_auth` - request-auth (WebAuthn) Blast radius if exploited: a forged `boarding_sweep_session` only authorizes exact approval tokens over a selection the real owner already WebAuthn-approved (bounded), but a forged `spend_approval` is a direct signing primitive. ## Fix Compare raw bytes with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, length-guarded: ```js const expectedSig = hmacSha256(tokenKey, bodyB64u); // Buffer const sigBuf = Buffer.from(sigB64u, "base64url"); if (sigBuf.length !== expectedSig.length || !timingSafeEqual(sigBuf, expectedSig)) { throw new Error("bad token signature"); } ``` Accept/reject semantics are **identical** — valid tokens still pass, invalid still fail — the comparison only becomes time-invariant. No API contract change. ## Why it breaks nothing The change is inside the one primitive all 6 token consumers route through. If it broke accept/reject, `proof:receive` would fail (it exercises valid + rejected tokens across every endpoint: WebAuthn auth, spend_approval sign, all three session tokens, boarding sweep 3-round flow, tree, mixed-auth 400, selection-bound 403). ## Tests - New `proof:token` isolates the new reject branches: tampered sig (1-bit flip), wrong-length sig, wrong key, expired. 5 checks. - Full self-contained suite green on this branch: - `proof:receive` ✓ (every token path) - `proof:api-send` ✓ - `proof:pending-swaps` ✓ (18 scenarios) - `proof:sqlite` ✓ - `proof:token` ✓ - `proof:health/version/deployment-bump/app` need live external services — not applicable here. ## Broader sweep (no other findings) Grepped every `!==` in `src/` against secret-ish field names. This was the **only** secret-string comparison: - WebAuthn assertion sig → Node `crypto.verify` (correct primitive) - `rpIdHash.equals()` → already constant-time Buffer compare, and rpIdHash is not a secret - All other `!==` are on public values (pubkeys, purpose strings, cred IDs, payment hashes) - No tokens/sigs/HMACs reach logs — only `truncate()`-d identifiers + counts ## Deploy Bumps `nuri_server_deployment_version` 3 → 4 (enforced by `deployment-bump-proof` as `config > live` gate). Will **not** auto-merge. Plan: deploy → verify one real tx end-to-end → then merge to main.

prompt_context.issue_body: ## Problem `/api/arkade/receive/sync` and `/api/arkade/receive/claim/approve` take ~5–6s each because both refresh **every** owner Lightning-receive row live — including terminal (dead) rows — and serially probe each failed row's reverse transaction. With `failed=10` historical rows, the one active claimable receive is stuck behind that work, so the passkey prompt appears ~20s after the user taps unlock. ## Change (server-side only, response shape preserved) - **`src/ArkadeReceive.js` — `buildLightningReceiveRows`**: partition dead-status rows (`invoice.expired`, `swap.expired`, `transaction.failed`, `transaction.refunded`) out up front. Dead state is terminal per Boltz, so these skip the live status fetch *and* the per-row reverse-tx probe entirely. They're kept as stored evidence (`status: "cleanup_needed"`), or purged when the caller passes `deleteCleanup`. Active rows (`swap.created` / `transaction.mempool` / `transaction.confirmed` / settled) still refresh live exactly as before. - **`src/ArkadeServer.js` — `requireReceiveClaimApprovalContext`**: refresh only the selected `swap_id` instead of resyncing the owner's whole receive history. Every security check is unchanged — owner scoping (`cred_id` + `client_public_key_33`), claimable-status gate, claim-key match, lockup-input + PSBT sign-request verification, and `receive_claim:<swap_id>` token scope. ## Safety / correctness - No funds are moved on either path; approval is still gated on ownership, claimability, sign requests, and lockup input. - Fails closed for wrong owner / wrong swap / wrong PSBT / unclaimable status. - Terminal rows are preserved as history (not deleted on the sync path). - Client-provided status is never trusted; stored status comes only from prior live Boltz fetches. ## Tests `npm run proof:receive`, `npm run proof:pending-swaps`, `npm run proof:local` all pass (incl. dead/failed scenarios S5–S8 and spent-VHTLC claim approval). ## Deploy / rollback - Bump `nuri_server_deployment_version` 4 → 5 before deploy (separate commit). - Test-deploy this branch to arkade.nuri.com, verify, then merge to main. linked_issues.body: ## Goal When a user logs in with an existing passkey on a new device, their arkade VTXOs, swap state, and contract metadata should restore automatically — same way the boarding address reappears today (which is already deterministic from the passkey PRF). Without this, signing into nuri on a second device produces an empty wallet that the SDK reconstructs from the indexer at best, and loses Lightning swap refund material at worst. ## Background — verified, not assumed The arkade boarding/ark addresses are fully deterministic and need no backup: - Client-Pk: `passkey_PRF(PRF_SALT) -> HKDF -> musig2.IndividualPubkey` (`services/arkade/ArkadeRemoteIdentity.ts:897-906`). Same passkey, same PRF, same client-pk. - Server-Pk: server-side BIP32-style derivation from `COSIGNER_SEED_V4 + clientPk` (`apis/server-2fa/v4/src/ArkadeDerive.js:222-247`, walletId logic at `:63-74`). Deterministic per client-pk. - Aggregated MuSig2 key (= boarding + ark address): computed from the two above. What is **not** deterministic and lives only in local AsyncStorage under prefix `nuri:arkade:v4:` (`services/arkade/ArkadeRecoveryBackupService.ts:38-46`): - `wallet:state`, `collection:contracts`, `collection:swaps`, `collection:reverseSwaps`, `collection:submarineSwaps`, `vtxos:*`, `utxos:*`, `tx:*`, `contract:*`. A server-side encrypted backup is already built end-to-end: - `installArkadeStorageObserver` patches `AsyncStorage.setItem/multiSet/...` and debounces uploads (`AUTO_BACKUP_DEBOUNCE_MS = 2_500`, `ArkadeRecoveryBackupService.ts:420`). - `buildPlaintext` packs storage + public context + passkey credId/credPubkey. - Encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305, key derived via `HKDF(passkey_PRF, KDF_SALT, \"nuri:arkade:recovery-backup:v1\")` — server cannot decrypt. - Mirrors to iCloud / Google Drive via `ArkadeCloudBackupService.ts`. **The gap:** `restoreArkadeRecoveryBackup()` at `ArkadeRecoveryBackupService.ts:890` is only called from `screens/debug/DebugArkadeModal.tsx`. No production code path triggers it. ## CredId / credPubkey flow on a fresh device — verified On existing-passkey login (\"Restore Wallet\"): - `useExistingWalletPasskey()` returns `{ prfB64, credIdB64u, isNew: false }` — **no `credPubkeyB64u`**. Confirmed iOS (`native-modules/ios/PasskeyModule.swift:593-597`) and Android (`PasskeyModule.kt:298-302`). This is WebAuthn-spec: assertions do not return the public key, only registrations do. - App.tsx `handleStatelessPayload:875` guard `if (payload.isNew && !hasCredPub)` does not trigger because `isNew === false`. - `statelessSignWalletFromPrf` persists `walletPasskeyCredIdB64u` correctly but writes `walletPasskeyCredPubkeyB64u = undefined` into `walletPublicKeys` (`AuthStateService.ts:520`). - Backup decrypt only needs `credIdB64u + PRF` (`ArkadeRecoveryBackupService.ts:598-632`) — both available. - `arkadeAuthBegin` accepts a missing `credPubkeyB64u` and falls back to `stored.credPubKeyB64u` (`ArkadeServer.js:849-868`); with the default `PASSKEY_PUBKEY_POLICY = soft` (`ArkadeConfig.js:68`) this is fine. If we ever switch to `hard` it breaks. Conclusion: technically nothing blocks restore on a fresh device today — we just never call it. ## Race condition to be aware of If `Wallet.create()` runs before restore (current behavior: `useArkadeSync` -> `getArkadeWalletSummary` -> `getOrCreateWallet` -> `Wallet.create()` with empty storage), the SDK writes fresh empty items into AsyncStorage. The auto-backup observer schedules an upload but **bails out** at `ArkadeRecoveryBackupService.ts:373` because `cachedKey + cachedAssertion` are not yet warm (no PRF prompt has happened). So far safe. The danger: as soon as the user performs an op that triggers a PRF prompt (e.g. send), the cache warms, the next storage write fires `runAutoRecoveryBackup`, which uploads the **fresh empty state** as the new backup. The old backup is overwritten. Data loss. → Restore must run **before** `Wallet.create()`, or we must explicitly suppress auto-backup until restore c
